title: Static normal force
description: Essential: The student must state or derive the correct expression for the normal/elastic force, N = mg cos α.

title: Static friction force
description: Essential: The student must state or derive the correct expression for the static friction force, f = mg sin α.

title: Kinetic friction coefficient
description: Essential: The student must state or derive the correct final answer for the coefficient of kinetic friction, μ = tan θ.

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution should correctly resolve gravity into components and apply Newton's first law for both the static and constant-velocity scenarios.

title: Distinguish static and kinetic
description: Important: The student must recognize that part (1) involves static equilibrium (friction adjusts to balance) and part (2) involves kinetic friction (constant velocity implies net force zero).

title: Free-body diagram logic
description: Optional: A clear free-body diagram or equivalent verbal description of all forces acting on the laptop on the incline.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The final expressions are checked for dimensional consistency (e.g., force has units of mg).

title: Confusing angle or force
description: Pitfall: Using sin α for the normal force or cos α for the friction force in the static equilibrium setup.

title: Misapplying friction relation
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly using the static friction result (tan α) as the kinetic friction coefficient, instead of deriving μ_k = tan θ from the constant-velocity condition.
